cards.explanation: The answer is the LORD. Eve says, “With the help of the LORD I have brought forth a man…” (Genesis 4:1). She has just given birth to Cain, and the LORD is the One she names. I bet a lot of names could cross a new mom's mind right then, and she goes straight to Him.

The answer is a keeper of sheep. Genesis 4:2 says Abel was a keeper of sheep. A shepherd works with a whole flock, and sheep never once ask for a raise. Hold on to that job, friends, because it comes back later in this story.

The answer is soil. Genesis 4:2 says Cain was a tiller of the soil, so he works the ground. Abel has the sheep and Cain has the soil. Tilling is turning the ground over so something can grow. Me, I turn dough over and hope for cookies. Cain's work gets him a harvest.
The answer is the best portions of the firstborn of his flock. Genesis 4:4 says Abel brought exactly that. A shepherd brings from the sheep he keeps. It lines up with his job from verse 2.

The answer is False. Genesis 4:4-5 says the LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering, but He had no regard for Cain and his offering. Both brothers brought something, and the LORD responds differently. The text doesn't say why in these verses, so I won't guess.
The answer is that he becomes very angry. Genesis 4:5 says Cain became very angry, and his countenance fell. That means his face dropped, friends. He doesn't hide it at all.

The answer is sin. The LORD says to Cain, “…sin is crouching at your door; it desires you, but you must master it.” (Genesis 4:7). Cain is already very angry by then (Genesis 4:5), and the LORD speaks to him before Cain kills Abel. Sin is the thing at the door, and the LORD says Cain must master it.
The answer is master. The LORD says, “it desires you, but you must master it.” (Genesis 4:7). Sin wants something from Cain, and Cain is told to master it. The LORD tells him this up front.
The answer is True. Genesis 4:8 says Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let us go out to the field.” So Cain starts the invitation. The next part of that verse is a hard one.

The answer is True. When the LORD asks, “Where is your brother Abel?” Cain answers, “I do not know!” (Genesis 4:9). He says it right to the LORD. It's a heavy moment, and the LORD keeps talking to him.
The answer is blood. The LORD says, “The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to Me from the ground.” (Genesis 4:10). The LORD hears it, friends. That's a heavy line, and it's all in the text.

The answer is False. The LORD tells Cain, “When you till the ground, it will no longer yield its produce to you.” (Genesis 4:12). Cain's work was the soil, so this lands right on his job. It's part of what the LORD says to him.

The answer is a fugitive and a wanderer. The LORD tells Cain, “You will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth.” (Genesis 4:12). A man who farmed one patch of ground is told he'll be on the move. I think that sounds like a hard road.
The answer is that whoever finds him will kill him. Cain tells the LORD, “…whoever finds me will kill me.” (Genesis 4:14). He says it out loud. I think this one hurts to hear.

The answer is a mark. Genesis 4:15 says, “And the LORD placed a mark on Cain, so that no one who found him would kill him.” The LORD answers Cain's fear with the mark. The text doesn't say what the mark looks like.

The answer is the land of Nod. Genesis 4:16 says Cain went out from the presence of the LORD and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden. Nod is the name of the place. That's where his new life starts.
The answer is a city. Genesis 4:17 says Cain built a city. Not a hut, not a shed, a whole city. I can barely keep my bakery counter clear of flour, so I'm impressed.

The answer is his son Enoch. Genesis 4:17 says Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch. Enoch was born to Cain and his wife in that same verse. A whole city with the boy's name on it. I bet that boy never had to spell his name at a restaurant.

The answer is Cain. Lamech says, “If Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold.” (Genesis 4:24). He brings Cain up by name. Back in Genesis 4:15 the LORD said that if anyone slays Cain, Cain will be avenged sevenfold. Lamech goes from seven to seventy-seven, and I think that's quite a jump.

The answer is Abel. Eve says, “God has granted me another seed in place of Abel, since Cain killed him.” (Genesis 4:25). She names Abel, and I think that means she hasn't forgotten him. The son she has just given birth to is Seth, and she says God granted him in place of Abel.
The answer is True. Genesis 4:26 says, “At that time men began to call upon the name of the LORD.” It comes right after Enosh, Seth's son, is born. The chapter ends on a good note, friends.
